items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024
items.q: I don’t know I don’t think Milt was playing with Dave but Milt would be there and that’s how I got to know him.

ctx.x: Milt Hinton and that crowd of people just seemed to have the kind of character that you want to emulate.

Well that time, that was in the ‘70s, and I had just moved here to 49th Street and I was so lucky because two of the best places for me as a singer and pianist were right within reach, that one on 55th just off Third Avenue, and then the other one Jimmy Weston’s, where I did get to work but I believe Gil Wiest is still alive, in his 90s, living out in Santa Monica. He was quite a character, not a kissy-huggy person at all but he had one of the best clubs going, and it was in the period of, I didn’t realize it at…

the Mad Men. He had that kind of crowd to come in and just eat the food and pay for the entertainment whether they cared about who was playing or not. And then he had all these jazz all-stars and I, sitting at the bar with a bartender who used to work on 52nd Street already getting my vibe and taking care of me, and always having a check near the one drink that I would have, so the boss would think that I was still drinking you know, and allowing me to sit there all night, and eventually, for whatever reason,…
